format: Anthropic skill-creator evals.json. Each eval runs with the skill and without, three runs each, graded on the expectations below with evidence. Rounds 1-2 (ids 1-5) inline the HTML in the prompt; round 3 (ids 6-9) passes a file path instead, with the defect buried in a long stylesheet under evals/files/round3/.

evals.name: contrast-failure-gets-a-ratio
evals.expected_output: Body text #4a4a4a on #1a1a1a is about 2.0:1, far below WCAG AA 4.5:1. The review must report the actual ratio computed by scripts/contrast.py, rank it as the top finding, and give a numeric fix (a foreground hex that reaches 4.5:1 or better on that background).
expectations: The review states a contrast ratio for body text on background, and it is between 1.9:1 and 2.2:1
The finding is ranked as the most severe on the page
The fix names a specific replacement color and the ratio it achieves, not 'increase contrast'
The transcript shows scripts/contrast.py or scripts/preflight.py was run before the judgment was written

evals.name: theme-only-color-is-caught
evals.expected_output: Two defects a reader would not see in one theme: --muted is defined only inside the dark media query, so .note has no color in light mode and inherits; and body sets no background, so the page borrows the host's. Both are exactly what scripts/preflight.py detects (theme-only-color, no-body-bg). The review must name both.
expectations: The review reports that --muted is defined only inside a theme block
The review reports that body has no background of its own
Both are framed as blocking, not as polish
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py was run

evals.name: clean-page-is-called-clean
evals.expected_output: The page is well-built but not flawless: a reviewer who looks will find a few real observed and computed issues (the 64ch measure runs ~87 characters; no lang, no color-scheme; a 48/64px frame). What is being tested is restraint in HOW findings are reported: severity chips and deductions attach only to computed or observed evidence, taste goes under an unranked Judgment calls section with no chip, and nothing is invented to fill the report.
expectations: Every severity-chipped finding carries [computed] or [observed] evidence; no chip sits on a [judged] item
Each chipped finding names its evidence class
Any subjective remark is labeled as a judgment call rather than a defect
Taste and preference remarks appear under a Judgment calls section with no severity chip

evals.name: asymmetry-gets-a-pixel-delta
evals.expected_output: The card's left padding is 18px against 24px on the other three sides. The review should measure it (scripts/symmetry.py on the rendered page, or read it from the CSS) and report the 6px delta with the fix, rather than describing it as 'feels unbalanced'.
expectations: The review names the left padding as 18px against 24px, or reports a 6px inset delta
The fix is numeric: set left padding to 24px, or equivalent
The review does not describe the problem only in sensory terms without the measurement

evals.name: unmeasurable-is-said-so
evals.prompt: Review this for craft. I can't share the source, only this description: a dashboard with a left nav, six KPI tiles in a 3x2 grid, a line chart below, and a table. Colors are a navy sidebar, white content area, blue accent.
evals.expected_output: There is nothing to measure. The skill's rule is to read exact values and compute before judging; with no values, it must say what it cannot assess and ask for the source, screenshot, or Figma link, rather than producing confident findings about spacing and contrast it has not seen.
expectations: The response states that it cannot measure spacing, contrast, or alignment from a verbal description
It asks for source, a screenshot, or a design file
It does not report any numeric finding
Any guidance offered is explicitly framed as general rather than as findings about this page

evals.name: buried-contrast-in-a-long-stylesheet
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round3/buried-contrast.html.
evals.expected_output: A 442-line settlements dashboard with a three-tier token system (primitive ramp, semantic role, component-scoped chip token). Exactly one text/background pair fails WCAG AA, and only in dark mode: the 'In review' status chip, `.ledger .pill--review`, resolves through --pill-warn-fg -> --amber-500 (#a8802f) on --pill-warn-bg -> --amber-950 (#3a2c10) = 3.74:1 against the 4.5:1 body minimum. It passes in light mode (#7a4a06 on #fbf1de = 6.67:1), so reading the base stylesheet alone will not find it, and the values are three var() hops from the hex. Every other pair on the page clears AA in both themes. scripts/preflight.py resolves tokens per theme and reports this one line.
expectations: The review reports a contrast failure on the .ledger .pill--review status chip in the dark theme, with a ratio between 3.0:1 and 4.3:1

No other TEXT contrast failure is reported: the other two chips, the buttons, the table header and body text are not flagged for text-on-background contrast (a finding about a control BORDER under WCAG 1.4.11 is correct and does not count)
The failure is scoped to dark mode rather than stated as failing everywhere
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py or scripts/contrast.py was run against the file
The fix names a specific replacement hex and the ratio it reaches on #3a2c10

evals.name: theme-only-token-buried-in-a-theme-layer
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round3/buried-theme-only.html.
evals.expected_output: A 422-line workspace settings screen. One custom property, --accent-edge, is declared only inside the dark `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block (line 254, in a theme layer appended at the end of the stylesheet) and never in the base :root or the [data-theme="dark"] block. It is read 67 lines earlier by `.notice`, the data-retention callout, as `border-left: 3px solid var(--accent-edge)`, so in light mode the border falls back to currentColor and the callout's accent edge disappears. body paints its own background, contrast clears AA in both themes, and every spacing value is on the 4/8 scale, so this is the only finding scripts/preflight.py returns.
expectations: The review reports that --accent-edge is defined only inside a dark theme block and never applies in the default light state
It names the component that reads the token (the .notice retention callout's left border) and what happens there in light mode
It is ranked blocking or critical, not polish
The token defect is ranked first among all findings, and any other finding ranked blocking carries a computed value rather than an impression
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py was run against the file

evals.name: one-off-scale-value-among-sixty
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round3/off-scale-once.html.
evals.expected_output: A 467-line support triage screen with 62 spacing declarations. Sixty-one are on the 4/8px scale. One is not: `.composer` (the reply box in the detail panel, line 247) uses `padding: 13px 17px`. Nothing else is wrong — contrast clears AA in both themes, body paints its own ground, no theme-only token. Finding it by eye means checking every padding, margin and gap on the page against the scale, which is exactly what scripts/preflight.py's off-scale check does in one pass.
expectations: The review reports 13px and 17px padding on .composer as off the 4/8px spacing scale
No other spacing value on the page is reported as off-scale
The fix is numeric: an on-scale replacement such as 12px 16px
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py was run against the file

evals.name: asymmetry-only-visible-after-layout
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round3/rendered-asymmetry.html.
evals.expected_output: A 311-line release-health page with three identical .kpi cards in a flex row. All three declare `padding: 24px`. The middle card carries `data-state="breached"`, which adds `border-left: 8px solid var(--alert)` as a status stripe; under `box-sizing: border-box` that eats 8px of the card's left padding box, so its content sits 32px from the card's left edge against 24px on both neighbors and the three labels no longer share a left edge. No single CSS value states 32px anywhere; it exists only after layout. `python3 scripts/symmetry.py <file>` renders the page headless and returns exactly one finding: a MAJOR paired-component mismatch, left inset 24px vs 32px. scripts/preflight.py is clean on this page.
expectations: The review reports that the breached KPI card's content starts 32px from its left edge against 24px on the two sibling cards, or names the 8px delta
It attributes the delta to the 8px border-left status stripe on the [data-state="breached"] card interacting with border-box sizing
The transcript shows scripts/symmetry.py was run on the HTML file, and the measurement is presented as computed rather than as an impression
The fix is numeric and preserves the stripe: reduce that card's left padding to 16px, or move the stripe to an inset box-shadow or pseudo-element so it costs no layout space

evals.name: alpha-only-contrast-failure
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round4/alpha-contrast.html.
evals.expected_output: A 281-line shipment console with no CSS custom properties anywhere — plain hex, one theme. Two things are being tested at once. First, a page with no tokens still gets a contrast pass at all: preflight.py used to skip the whole contrast check when a document declared no custom properties, so a plain-CSS page was never measured. Second, the one failure only exists after alpha compositing: `.stamp` (the relative timestamp beside each timeline event) sets `color: rgba(52, 64, 84, 0.65)` on `background: #eef1f6`. Composited that is 3.62:1 against AA's 4.5 for 12px text. Read as an opaque #344054 — which is what dropping the alpha does — it is 9.24:1 and passes with room to spare, so the defect is invisible to anyone eyeballing the declared hex. Every other pair on the page clears 6.5:1 or better, and preflight.py returns this single line and nothing else.
expectations: The review reports a contrast failure on the .stamp timestamp, with a ratio between 3.4:1 and 3.9:1
The finding attributes the failure to the 0.65 alpha being composited over #eef1f6, not to the declared color value on its own
No other text contrast pair on the page is reported as failing (the chips, buttons, table header, card notes and footer all clear AA)
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py or scripts/contrast.py was run against the file
The fix is numeric: a specific replacement alpha or hex, with the ratio it reaches on #eef1f6 (for example rgba(52,64,84,0.8) = 5.33:1, or #525c70 = 5.94:1)

evals.name: dark-only-token-is-not-a-defect
evals.prompt: Review this page for design quality. The full source is at evals/files/round4/legit-theme-token.html.
evals.expected_output: A 264-line digest page with a correct two-state token system: the base :root carries the light palette and a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block overrides it. Ten tokens are declared in base and overridden in dark. Two more — --lift-shadow and --hairline-warm — are declared ONLY inside the dark block, and are read only by rules inside that same block (.card and .aside). That is correct: a lifted shadow and a warmed hairline have no light-mode counterpart, and neither token is ever referenced from a state where it would not resolve. This is the false-positive guard for eval 7's check. preflight.py returns 'clean: no showstoppers' — zero blocking, zero warnings — and the earlier version of the theme-only-color rule, which blocked any token absent from base, reported both of these as BLOCK findings and ranked the false positive first.
expectations: Neither --lift-shadow nor --hairline-warm is reported as a defect for being declared only inside the dark theme block
No finding claims a custom property on this page fails to resolve in the default light state
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py was run against the file, and the review reflects that it returned no blocking findings
If the dark-only tokens are discussed at all, they are described as correct because they are read only by rules inside the same dark block
Any finding that is reported carries a computed or observed value rather than an impression

floors: contrast-failure-gets-a-ratio: both arms 1.00. The baseline computes WCAG ratios unaided when the hex values are in the prompt.
asymmetry-gets-a-pixel-delta: both arms 1.00. The 18px/24px values are readable from the inline CSS without a script.
round-1 (2026-08-21, Opus 5).design-gap: Inline HTML hands the baseline every value, so measuring is trivial without scripts. The skill's edge only shows where a reader cannot see the defect (theme-only-color, +0.33 headline). A second-generation set needs inputs where values are not in the prompt: a long stylesheet with the defect buried, or a rendered screenshot.
defect-found: unmeasurable-is-said-so: with 0.50 vs without 1.00. The skill scored and severity-tagged a page it never saw. Fixed (Inputs item 5, Section 6); re-run as round 2.

clean-page-is-called-clean: both arms fail the judgment-labeling check. The skill tags taste [judged] and still chips it Major. Fixed (Section 6); re-run as round 2. If the baseline still fails 6/6 after round 2, the expectation itself may be miscalibrated.
grader-fixes: 'no numeric finding' moved to a reader: citing 4.5:1 as a standard is not a finding

round-2 (2026-08-21).clean-page-is-called-clean: Round-1 expectations E1/E4 rewarded not-looking: they assumed the fixture was flawless. Round-2 with-skill runs chipped only [computed]/[observed] items (87-char measure, no lang/color-scheme, 48/64 frame, theme contrast mismatch), all real, and quarantined [judged] items unchipped under Judgment calls, which is the rule the fix encodes. Expectations recalibrated to test that rule. The fixture itself is a round-3 item: make it actually pass a full review, or keep it as is and test reporting discipline, which is what it now does.
round-2 (2026-08-21).unmeasurable-is-said-so: With-skill 6/6 on the judgment checks, up from 0/6. All three refuse to score a description and quarantine guidance.
round-2 (2026-08-21).voice-sample-precedence (natural-writing: With-skill 3/3; dashes per draft 5/5/4 against round 1's 7/5/1.

round-3 (2026-08-21).design: Answers round 1's design-gap note. Each fixture is a 300-470 line page whose values cannot be held in the reader's head: tokens resolve through two or three var() hops, defects sit 150-290 lines down, and the prompt carries a path rather than the source. Every fixture was verified so the bundled script returns the plant and nothing else — preflight.py for ids 6-8, symmetry.py (headless Chromium) for id 9, which preflight cannot see at all.

plants.6: .ledger .pill--review, dark theme only, #a8802f on #3a2c10 = 3.74:1 (WARN, not a dramatic 1.5:1)
plants.7: --accent-edge declared only in the dark @media block, read by .notice 67 lines earlier
plants.8: .composer padding: 13px 17px, the only off-scale pair among 62 spacing declarations
plants.9: 8px border-left stripe on the middle .kpi card; content inset 32px vs 24px, visible only after layout

notes.round-3/4 correction (2026-08-21): round-3/4 correction (2026-08-21): expectation 4 of this eval originally read 'No other blocking defect is reported: no contrast failure, no off-scale spacing, no missing body background'. That encoded a false premise: the fixture also has form-control borders at 1.53:1 light / 1.27:1 dark (WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3:1) and no layout breakpoint at all, both real blocking defects the fixture author never planted and preflight.py does not check. Reporting them is correct, so the expectation was rewarding not-looking, the same defect round 2 found in clean-page-is-called-clean. It now tests ranking discipline instead. Round 3 was re-graded on the new wording so both rounds use one yardstick.
notes.round-3 correction, expectation 2 of eva: Originally 'No other contrast failure is reported: the other two chips, the buttons, the table header, and body text are not flagged'. One run flagged the .btn--quiet BORDER, which resolves to #cfd6e0 on #fcfcfd = 1.43:1 light and #27313f on #161d26 = 1.29:1 dark, both under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 wants for a control boundary. That finding is correct. The expectation meant text contrast and now says so. Third false premise of this kind in this eval set; every one came from verifying a fixture only with the tool under test.

round-4 (2026-08-21).design: Two fixtures for checks added the same day and previously untested. Eval 10 is a positive case for two script changes at once (alpha compositing in contrast.py, and contrast running on a page with no custom properties in preflight.py). Eval 11 is a negative case: a legitimate theme-scoped token that the earlier theme-only-color rule flagged, which is the false positive the rule was narrowed to stop.

plants.10: .stamp color rgba(52,64,84,0.65) on #eef1f6 = 3.62:1 composited, 9.24:1 if the alpha is dropped; no custom properties anywhere on the page
plants.11: no plant — --lift-shadow and --hairline-warm are declared and consumed entirely inside the dark block, and preflight.py must stay silent

round-4 (2026-08-21).guard: Eval 11 fails if the theme-only-color check is ever widened back to 'defined in a theme block and not in base'. Verified by re-running that earlier predicate against the fixture: it reports both tokens as BLOCK.

notes.round-4 note on eval 11 (2026-08-21): dark-only-token-is-not-a-defect is a REGRESSION GUARD, not a discriminator, and its headline delta should not be read as a behavioral win. Neither arm reports the dark-only tokens as defects; the baseline's only failure is the check that preflight.py was run, which no arm without the skill can pass. Its job is to fail loudly if a future change re-breaks the theme check, which today's narrowing did in one form and this morning's did in another.
